Natural Earth Russia without Kaliningrad, Tuva, the Kurils, southern Sakhalin, the Karelian Isthmus and Ladoga Karelia (Finnish until 1940). The shape is the RSFSR proper; Turkestan (30 April 1918) and the Kirghiz ASSR (26 August 1920) were autonomous republics inside the RSFSR and are ledger vassals, not drawn here. Cliopatria draws Russia inside its Russian Republic (22.3 M km2 in 1917, 17.9 M in 1918), Republics of the Soviet Union (21.5 M, 1920-21) and USSR shapes. Only the core is Soviet-held at first (the page does not date the spread of Soviet power); the shape is the claim until the Czechoslovak revolt of May-August 1918, which the next keyframes subtract.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1918, the Soviet-held land at the year's end. The Czechoslovak Legion's revolt (Chelyabinsk 14 May; Samara and the Komuch, formed 8 June; the Provisional Siberian Government at Omsk, 13 June; Syzran, Tyumen and Irkutsk in July; the Allied landing at Vladivostok 3 August) and the Russian State founded at Ufa on 23 September take Siberia, the Urals and the Far East away (ledger, June-September 1918); Syzran and Samara are regained on 3 and 8 October and Perm is lost on 24 December 1918 (ledger). The Don, Kuban and North Caucasus stay inside as the Soviet claim until South Russia is set up on 8 January 1919. No page gives an area; the regions are those the russian-state and far-eastern-republic dossiers draw. Replaces the single 1917-1939 keyframe, which drew all of Russia through the Civil War.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1919, the Soviet-held land at the year's end (the spring Kolchak offensive that took Ufa and the Udmurt towns and the autumn White peak at Orel and Voronezh are carried by the ledger). Ufa, Yekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk are regained in June-July, Omsk on 14 November and the rest of Western Siberia in November-December (ledger); South Russia holds the Don, Kuban, North Caucasus and the Crimea until January-November 1920 (south-russia 1919 keyframe, the October peak); the Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates pass from the Byelorussian SSR to the RSFSR in February-April 1919 and the Gomel Governorate is created on 26 April 1919 (Byelorussian SSR page). No page gives an area.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1920. Irkutsk and Krasnoyarsk are regained in January-March 1920, Rostov in January, Novorossiysk and the Kuban by April, the Crimea on 17 November (ledger). The Far Eastern Republic (6 April 1920) is a buffer state that the RSFSR does not own until the merger of 15 November 1922: its land (Transbaikal, Amur, the Maritime Province) is subtracted for 1920-1922, because nothing in the ledger gives it to the RSFSR before then (the Far East was lost in August 1918, ledger). Petsamo is ceded to Finland by the Treaty of Tartu of 14 October 1920 and drops out from 1921. Northern Taurida, held by Wrangel in 1920, is Ukrainian SSR land (south-russia dossier).

1918: the capital moves from Petrograd to Moscow (infobox: Petrograd 1917-1918, Moscow 1918-1991).

region.text: Russia proper as the Soviet claim of 1917 (the same shape as keyframe russian-soviet-federative-socialist-republic_1917): without Kaliningrad, Tuva, the Kurils, southern Sakhalin, the Karelian Isthmus and Ladoga Karelia

ledger.note: 1917 November to 1918 February: Soviet power is set up across Russia proper. October Revolution page, takeover dates: 'Saratov' 9 November 1917, 'Tver' 10 November, 'Tsaritsyn' 27 November, 'Petrozavodsk' 17 January 1918, 'Odessa and Orenburg' 31 January, 'Astrakhan' 7 February, 'Kiev and Vologda' 8 February, 'Arkhangelsk' 17 February 1918; the attempts 'were largely successful in Russia proper'. The event takes only land nobody holds. Confidence 2: the page lists towns, not a boundary, so the region is the Soviet claim of the 1917 keyframe. [fx-21 2026-11-01: new event. The Russian Republic's land passes to this state at the end of 1917 as Cliopatria's 1918 Russian Republic shape, which leaves 9,012 cells of the 1918 Soviet heartland (Arkhangelsk, Vologda, Kirov, Tver, Saratov, Karelia and the Samara-Syzran area) with nobody until the 1918 keyframe adds them (7,556 cells); the June and July 1918 losses of Samara and Syzran (ledger /4, /7) also moved nothing for the same reason. See the handoff on russian-republic.]

region.text: Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, most of Belarus and Ukraine, as the treaty page names them

ledger.note: 1918, 3 March: Brest-Litovsk: Soviet Russia "gave up claims to Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, most of Belarus, and Ukraine" and returned Kars, Ardahan and Batum to the Ottomans. The page cites 34% of the population, 54% of industrial land and 89% of coalfields lost. Soviet control of these lands was nominal; the treaty was annulled on 13 November 1918. The page says "The territory of the Kingdom of Poland was not mentioned in the treaty". [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: Poland is dropped from the region (it was never inside the keyframes and the page does not name it); confidence stays 2 after the reviewer's change from 3.]

region.text: Transcaspia regained by 1920; Bukhara and Khiva stand beside it as people's republics (enclaves, TA/BP)

ledger.note: 1918, 30 April: the Turkestan ASSR is formed inside the RSFSR; it is the RSFSR's autonomous republic until it is disbanded on 27 October 1924.

1918, June: the Czechoslovak Legion "captured Samara" in June (the page gives no day), which enabled "the first anti-Bolshevik local government in Siberia, the Komuch, formed on 8 June". [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: the summer-1918 loss of the Volga land that the russian-state dossier is founded on.]

1918, 13 June: "On 13 June, Whites formed the Provisional Siberian Government in Omsk" after White officers' organizations overthrew the Bolsheviks there (no date); the Legion "quickly occupied" Petropavl, Kurgan, Novonikolaevsk and Mariinsk and "took Tyumen" in July. Confidence 2: the date and the base are the page's, the extent (Western Siberia) is the researcher's reading, as in russian-state /ledger/0 and /ledger/5. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event.]
1918, July: the constitution gives the state its name, the Russian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic (RSFSR); the page gives no day.
1918, July: White Russian troops under Kappel "took Syzran" (the page gives only the month); the Komuch's People's Army. Syzran is regained on 3 October 1918. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event.]

1918, July: "Radola Gajda took Irkutsk" with the Czechoslovak forces; the Legion also "quickly occupied" Nizhneudinsk and Kansk after Chelyabinsk. Confidence 2: Irkutsk is dated to the month; the rest of the Krasnoyarsk region is the researcher's reading from Kansk. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event.]

region.text: the Far East: Transbaikal, Amur, the Maritime Province

ledger.note: 1918, 3 August: Japanese, British, French and American troops "landed at Vladivostok" (the page does not say when Soviet power fell in the Far East). The Far East then has no state: the Allied and Japanese forces, Semyonov's Transbaikal regime and the Russian State's "almost nominal" Far East district hold it until the Far Eastern Republic of April 1920; empire-of-japan /ledger/28 records the Japanese occupation of the Maritime Provinces from 8 August 1918. The region is the Far Eastern Republic's 1922 land. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: the reviewer found no loss of the Far East before the 1922 merge.]

region.text: the Urals, Sverdlovsk (Yekaterinburg), Chelyabinsk and Orenburg

ledger.note: 1918, 23 September: the Ufa Act makes the Provisional All-Russian Government "the sole bearer of the supreme power in the whole space of the Russian state" (russian-state /ledger/0); the Urals and Orenburg were already outside Soviet control (the Czech revolt page dates only Chelyabinsk, 14 May 1918) and are counted from the founding of the state; the pages opened give no 1918 dates for Yekaterinburg or Orenburg. Ufa, where the Act was signed, is left out: the Red Army held it again before the Whites retook it on 14 March 1919 (event below, russian-state /ledger/11), and no page opened dates the 1918 Red retaking. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: the Urals part of the summer-1918 losses.] [fx-21 2026-11-01: Sverdlovsk and Chelyabinsk oblasts added. Eastern Front (Russian Civil War) page: the Provisional Regional Government of the Urals was formed 'in Yekaterinburg on 25 August 1918'; Revolt of the Czechoslovak Legion page: 'In May 1918, soldiers of the Czechoslovak Legion revolted against the Bolsheviks in Chelyabinsk' (14 May). Without them the Russian State's found claim on these oblasts lost to this dossier under rule R2 (2,168 cells in 1918) and this dossier's 1918 keyframe had to release them (Sverdlovsk 687, Chelyabinsk 284). Ufa and Bashkortostan stay out, as above.]
1918, 3 and 8 October: the Directory forces abandon Syzran (3 October) and Samara (8 October) to the Red Army.
1918, 21-24 December: the White Siberian Army takes Kungur (21 December) and Perm (24 December).

region.text: the Don, the Kuban and the North Caucasus

ledger.note: 1919, 8 January: South Russia is established by the White movement on the Don, the Kuban and the North Caucasus (south-russia /ledger/0); the Soviet claim on this land ends. Confidence 2: the page lists the territory without dates; the founding core is a reading. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: mirror of the south-russia found event, which names the RSFSR as counterpart.]

1919, February-April: the Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates pass to the RSFSR (the page ties the transfer to the Litbel decision of 28 February 1919; no day). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: mirror of byelorussian-soviet-socialist-republic /ledger/4; the transfer also changes this dossier's shape 1919-1924.]

region.text: Ufa and the Udmurt and Bashkir towns, March-April 1919

ledger.note: 1919, 14 March: the White Western Army occupies Ufa; in April it takes Sarapul, Votkinsk, Izhevsk, Belebey, Birsk, Bugulma and Buguruslan.

1919, 26 April: "the Gomel Governorate is created" inside the RSFSR (the page does not say where its land came from, so the counterpart is nobody). Gomel returns to the Byelorussian SSR on 6 December 1926 (below). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: the Gomel part of the shape of 1919-1926.]

1919, May: the AFSR offensive "forced the front to retreat from" Kharkov, Belgorod, Balashov and Tsaritsyn (no day on the page). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: mirror of south-russia (Belgorod).]

1919, June: "In June 1919, after a fierce battle, Wrangel's troops stormed and captured the heavily fortified city" (Tsaritsyn, now Volgograd). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: mirror of south-russia (the former /ledger/0 had put Tsaritsyn against the Ukrainian SSR).]
1919, 9 June: "The Red Army retook Ufa"; in July the Whites leave Yekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk (25 July), and the Urals pass to the Reds.

union.text: the Urals ridge and both slopes left with the withdrawal to the Trans-Urals

region.text: the Urals and Bashkir lands taken in the spring offensive, the Sverdlovsk and Chelyabinsk oblasts and the Urals region left with the withdrawal to the Trans-Urals

ledger.note: 1919, summer: the Urals west of the Trans-Urals line (Perm, Kungur, the Udmurt towns, Orenburg approaches) pass to the Reds with the Siberian Army's retreat. Bridging: the pages date only Ufa (9 June), Yekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk (July) and the withdrawal "to the Trans-Urals"; Perm, Izhevsk and Sarapul are not dated. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: mirror of russian-state /ledger/15 (confidence 1, flagged).] [fx-21 2026-11-01: the Urals region added to the region, mirror of russian-state /ledger/15 (the circles around the cities left about 1,330 cells of it, and 1,150 of them were added by this dossier's 1919 keyframe). Russian State page: 'the whole of the Ural was occupied' in the April 1919 offensive; June-July the Siberian army 'withdrew to the Trans-Urals', 'Ekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk were left'.] [fx-21 2026-11-01: the Sverdlovsk and Chelyabinsk oblasts added as well, the same two the RSFSR dossier takes from the state in September 1918 (/11); the 100 km circles of /13 left 584 and 182 of their cells with the state. Russian State page: 'Ekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk were left' in July 1919.]

1919, September: the Southern Front gave up "Kiev, Odessa, Kursk, Voronezh, and Orel between August and October" and "through September and early October the front retreated to the north again"; the page gives no day for Kursk. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: mirror of south-russia (Kursk was RSFSR land).]
1919, 30 September: the Armed Forces of South Russia take Voronezh and Orel; Kharkov, Tsaritsyn, Kiev and Kursk had fallen earlier in 1919.

region.text: the Kirghiz ASSR, later the Kazakh ASSR

region.text: Sevastopol, which held out until 3 July 1942

region.text: the Don, the Kuban and the North Caucasus of 1942

region.text: the Don, the Kuban and the North Caucasus of 1942

region.text: southern Sakhalin (Karafuto) and the Kuril Islands

union.text: the Don, the Kuban and the North Caucasus of 1942

notes: No Cliopatria row for the republic as such: Cliopatria draws Russia inside Russian Republic (1917-1919), Republics of the Soviet Union (1920-1921) and Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (1922-1991); this dossier is the RSFSR as an internal unit (the Russian Federation's Cliopatria row starts 1992). It counts 14 pages, over the 5-page budget, because the Civil War events mirror the Russian State, South Russia and Far Eastern Republic dossiers, whose pages are cited. Not settled: (1) the spread of Soviet power Nov 1917-spring 1918 (no page dates it); (2) the Karelian Isthmus and the Ladoga shore went to the Karelo-Finnish SSR in March 1940 and to the Leningrad Oblast in September 1944 (the Karelo-Finnish page), so the RSFSR draws them only from September 1944; the Rybachy peninsula, Salla and the Gulf of Finland islands are not placed by any page; (3) Petsamo (ceded by Finland in 1944) and Hanko are not on the pages opened; (4) the Estonian and Latvian strips are circles of 25 km (Pechory), 20 km (Pytalovo) and 8 km (Ivangorod), the gazetteer lacking the names, and are dated 1944 (Abrene) and January-1945 (Ivangorod, Petseri) by the Latvian and Estonian pages; (5) Turkestan and the Kazakh lands are autonomous republics shown as vassal tints of the RSFSR, matching the turkestan-assr dossier; (6) the infobox area (17,125,200 km2, 1956 estimate "citation needed") is the only figure; (7) which Soviet leader list to use (the page lists Lenin as first head of government 1917-1924 and Boris Yeltsin as last), so no rulers strip is given.
